name: The mystery in four parts
hint: The crime, the investigation, the turn and the solution, with a second crime at the midpoint and an answer the reader can work out.

parts.title: The crime
chapters: The crime
(ca 8 %) The crime is discovered here, or within the first tenth of the book, so who and why are asked at once.
The detective
(ca 5-12 %) Show who investigates, why it has to be them, and what they carry that the case will press on.
The scene
(ca 10 %) The place, the body and the first finds. Hide the decisive clue here, in passing.
The circle
(ca 15 %) Introduce the suspects, each with motive, opportunity and something to hide. The culprit is already among them.

parts.title: The investigation
chapters: The interviews
(ca 20-35 %) Everyone lies about something. Let the detective catch one lie and miss another.
The first theory
(ca 35-45 %) An obvious suspect emerges, so the reader believes they are a step ahead.
The red herring
(ca 45 %) A true detail points the wrong way, and the detective and the reader both follow it.
A second crime
(ca 50 %) The midpoint: a new crime or discovery shatters the first theory and raises the stakes.

parts.title: The turn
chapters: It gets personal
(ca 55-65 %) The case comes close to the detective and threatens a relationship, a career or their sense of self.
The false solution
(ca 75 %) The wrong person is arrested or the case is closed. It looks settled, but one detail does not fit.
The detective in danger
(ca 80-85 %) The culprit realises the truth is close and strikes back.
The decisive clue
(ca 85-90 %) Something the reader has seen all along takes on a new meaning, and the detective understands.

parts.title: The solution
chapters: The confrontation
(ca 90 %) Detective and culprit meet with something at stake, and the solution plays out as a scene.
The reveal
(ca 95 %) How it was done and why, briefly, with the last pieces the reader has not already placed.
Afterwards
(ca 98 %) What the case cost, who the detective is now, and what lies ahead.
